newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Five killed as Nigerian feud shifts to new town.
newsitem.headline: Five killed as Nigerian feud shifts to new town.

text.p: Five people were killed, including a 75-year-old man who was beheaded, as ethnic clashes in the oil-producing midwestern part of Nigeria spread to another town, newspapers reported on Friday.
The semi-official Daily Times said grenade-throwing youths on Wednesday night invaded Koko town near Warri which had been the scene of clashes until troops deployed there on Tuesday.

"Five persons, among them a beheaded 75-year-old man, were killed in the attack following which hundreds of residents fled for safer areas," the paper said. "Grenades and dynamite were freely used in the attack."
Newspapers said many houses were set ablaze and the hospital in the town was damaged. A gas pumping station belonging to the Nigerian Gas Company was sacked, forcing the workers to flee.
Defence headquarters spokesman Colonel Godwin Ugbo said he could not confirm the report.
"Peace has returned to Warri and the officer on ground knows what to do if the crisis spreads to a neighbouring town," he told Reuters in Lagos.

Warri, 300 kms (190 miles) east of Lagos, has been the centre of communal fighting for the last month between militant youths over the transfer of the local council headquarters from an Ijaw town to a town of the rival Itsekiri tribe.

At the height of the crisis in March, armed Ijaw tribesmen occupied six oil flow stations of the Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group, shutting off 100,000 barrels per day of its crude oil production.
Some 127 of Shell's Nigerian staff held by the tribesmen were released after negotiations and oil production resumed.
A Shell spokesman said on Friday that there had been no change in the company's operations.
"Warri River flow station is still closed with the loss of 2,000 barrels per day," said Precious Omuku. The station was shut last weekend because of the clashes.
At the root of the crisis is a long-standing rivalry among three tribes -- the Ijaws, the Itsekiris and the Urhobos.
